note: Candidates only. DF21 passes when the author adopts one into results/manifests/nonobvious_finding.json after review. Every statement here is model behavior under tier-5 illustrative inputs unless its evidence line names a frozen snapshot; none is a claim about the world. Candidates are suspended rather than deleted when a later defect finding undercuts them, so the record shows what was believed and why it changed.

candidates.statement: The public-benchmark stop-the-line result (coverage 91% to 42%, 98.9% abstention, ~1% exposure) depends on per-wavelength standardization with eight PLS components; a standard SNV pipeline without that standardization shows a milder collapse (coverage 0.79 at 8 components, 0.72 at CV-selected components) and a gate that releases 40-60% of shifted tablets with 14-29% conditional error. In every mode the gate is not operationally useful under shift.
candidates.evidence: results/release_assurance/ra_*/metrics.json (three modes, 50 seeds each, bootstrap intervals); docs/methods/release_benchmark.md
candidates.changes_design: Release-assurance scenarios remain R0 in the base case; any R3 parameterization must name the pipeline; the repository's public claim needs the caveat (CLAIMS_REGISTER C005, C006).

candidates.statement: Chemical real-time release cannot shorten batch release for an aseptically filled solution while the 14-day sterility incubation is the critical path; in the engine a fully validated R3 layer saves zero days (test_full_release_assurance_saves_no_days_when_sterility_binds), and saves days only when rapid sterility and environmental monitoring are validated.
candidates.changes_design: H7 is testable and leans negative for the first archetype; S6's value hinges on the rapid-micro package, not the chemical layer.
candidates.status: candidate; consistent with the repository's own 2026-07-24 memo, so partly known internally

candidates.statement: Under the study's own illustrative inputs the frozen comparators do not fail for the reason the thesis assumes. For sodium bicarbonate the status-quo plant is specified above 100% utilization (1.245), so S0 and S1 fail on chronic capacity alone: sizing nominal capacity to 75% utilization moves mean fill from 0.720 to 0.973 and 0.728 to 0.982 without touching any resilience mechanism. For norepinephrine the status quo already sits at 0.778 utilization and fails only the tail, and the tail is set by the regional review rule: switching the regions from the frozen reorder-at-lane-time-plus-one-day rule to a daily base-stock review moves P(fill >= 0.99) from 0.56 to 0.90 for S0 and 0.65 to 0.94 for S1. Neither result is about distributed manufacturing.
candidates.evidence: results/ablation/abl_20260902_phaseA/summary.json keys base|*, loo:capacity_shortfall|*, loo:inventory_timing|*; meta.status_quo_utilization; 100 common-random-number runs per configuration
candidates.changes_design: Any comparison of architectures has to fix the scaffold first: capacity sized to a stated utilization and an inventory policy that is a policy rather than an artifact. Otherwise every added-capacity strategy wins trivially and every inventory strategy loses trivially. The session-1 conclusion that no strategy is feasible for norepinephrine was a model artifact.
candidates.status: candidate; the capacity and review-rule results stand (they are measured on the base world), but the cost ordering in NF-8 that follows from them is suspended pending the MD-4 to MD-14 fixes

candidates.statement: For the distributed-node strategies the binding constraint in the model is the commissioning window, not the running economics. With the illustrative 730-day commissioning inside a five-year evaluation window, S5 and S6 reach P(fill >= 0.99) of 0.00 for sodium bicarbonate; with commissioning removed they reach 0.99. Ten-year evaluation recovers only part of it (0.00 to 0.00 for sodium bicarbonate, 0.72 to 0.77 for norepinephrine), so the effect is the lost service during construction rather than the amortization of capital.
candidates.evidence: results/ablation/abl_20260902_phaseA/summary.json keys loo:commissioning_delay|*|S5 and loo:horizon_10y|*|S5 against base|*|S5
candidates.changes_design: A distributed architecture that must build before it serves is compared unfairly against strategies that scale an existing plant instantly (S2, S4 through capacity_factor). Either every strategy pays its true lead time or none do. This is a fair-comparison rule the protocol states (FC4) but the comparators do not honor symmetrically.

candidates.statement: The 503B responder strategy's service is dominated by legal availability rather than by capacity or cost: holding the product on the shortage list for the whole horizon moves P(fill >= 0.99) from 0.19 to 0.95 for sodium bicarbonate and 0.21 to 0.94 for norepinephrine, the largest single-mechanism effect measured for any strategy.
candidates.changes_design: It confirms in the model what the repository's regulatory memos argue in law: 503B capacity is a function of a time-varying legal state, so it can be a revenue bridge but never the durable architecture. A design that depends on it is depending on the shortage continuing.

candidates.statement: Release-time mechanisms are not what limits service for either product in this model. Zeroing the chemical, endotoxin, environmental-monitoring, and QA-review components together moves mean fill by at most 0.003 and P(fill >= 0.99) by at most 0.07; zeroing the 14-day sterility incubation moves mean fill by at most 0.006. Both are smaller than the effect of the inventory review rule for every strategy tested.
candidates.evidence: results/ablation/abl_20260902_phaseA/summary.json keys loo:release_queue|* and loo:sterility_delay|* against base|*
candidates.changes_design: It sharpens NF-2 from a mechanism argument to a measured one, and it says the release layer's value has to be argued on shelf life, distribution radius, or quality-workflow cost rather than on shortage days avoided.

candidates.statement: Under the illustrative inputs, fixed cost dominates every architecture and the status quo itself is already priced far above the market the products sell into. Fixed and resilience cost (annualized capital, fixed quality labor, validation, reservation fees, operating-system integration) is 81% to 95% of annual cost for all eight comparators, and the break-even price per delivered unit is 14.41 USD for the status quo and 41.05 to 53.37 USD for the distributed-node strategies. The repository's own primary-source price evidence for norepinephrine is 1.47 USD per vial on the VA Federal Supply Schedule Big4 price and 4.52 USD FSS (research/beachhead-verification.md, 2026-07-16). The model's status quo is therefore an order of magnitude above the price its product commands, which means the absolute economics in this package are not calibrated to a commodity sterile injectable and only the relative ordering of strategies carries information.
candidates.evidence: results/design_space/contract_conditions_sim_20260902T043039Z.csv (fixed_share_of_cost, break_even_price_usd_per_unit, resilience_premium_usd_per_unit) built by scripts/build_contract_table.py from results/simulation/sim_20260902T043039Z/summary.json; inputs capital_usd_per_site 40,000,000 USD and annual_demand_units 1,200,000 in config/products/*.yaml, both tier 5; price evidence from research/beachhead-verification.md lines 49 and 55
candidates.changes_design: Every cost conclusion in this package is a statement about the scaffold until node capital, fixed quality labor, and demand come from evidence (HA-11, HA-13). It also reframes the commercial question: at 81% to 95% fixed cost, utilization and contracted volume decide the economics, not process efficiency, which is what the portfolio, virtual-network, and take-or-pay families are for. A resilience premium of 12 to 40 USD per unit against a 1.47 USD vial is not a pricing question, it is a question of who pays for capacity that is not used.

candidates.statement: Correcting the two scaffold artifacts together makes the cheapest architecture feasible and leaves distributed manufacturing dominated. With nominal capacity sized to 75% utilization and regional inventory reviewed daily to a base-stock target, and nothing else changed, sodium bicarbonate S1 (one plant plus six months of safety stock) reaches mean fill 0.999 with P(fill >= 0.99) = 0.97 at 14.1 M USD/yr and 11.22 USD per delivered unit, which is both feasible at the frozen target and the cheapest strategy in the set; S2 (dual source) also clears at 24.9 M and 19.88 USD/unit; the four-node distributed strategies S5 and S6 do not clear (0.87) and cost 64.4 M and 67.5 M, or 51.68 and 54.17 USD per unit. Adding a free commissioning window lifts S5 and S6 to 0.99 but leaves them at 4.6 times S1's cost. The same ordering holds for norepinephrine, where the status quo itself (S0) becomes feasible at 0.91 once the review rule is fixed. In this model, after the artifacts are removed, inventory at an adequately sized plant dominates distributed manufacturing on both service and cost.
candidates.evidence: results/ablation/abl_20260902_phaseA_pairs/summary.json, configurations pair:capacity_shortfall+inventory_timing and pair:capacity_shortfall+inventory_timing+commissioning_delay against base, 100 common-random-number runs per configuration, tau 0.99, q 0.90, designs from opt_20260902T043854Z; costs are annual_total_cost.mean and cost_per_delivered_unit.mean in the same file
candidates.changes_design: It reverses the direction of the study's central question under its own inputs: the comparison the protocol asks for (can distributed capacity beat safety stock, dual sourcing, reserved capacity, or added central capacity) answers no for both products once the scaffold is corrected, and answers it by a wide margin rather than a close one. It also identifies exactly what would have to be true for the answer to change: inventory has to become expensive or impossible (short shelf life, high carrying cost, expiry), or the failure has to be something inventory cannot cover (a long total loss of the single plant, a demand shock larger than the stock, or a product whose demand cannot be forecast), or the node cost has to fall by roughly a factor of four. Those are the conditions Phase E should map and the evidence the founder should buy first.
candidates.status: candidate; SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06 by revisions R009 to R011 and the full-resolution re-evaluation. Charging for opening inventory (NEW-1) and giving the frozen comparators the same inventory search space (MD-3, MD-12) moved the feasible set: distributed nodes now clear for norepinephrine at a tail probability of 0.940, dual sourcing clears at 0.960, and the deep-stock winners lose feasibility for sodium bicarbonate. See docs/design_space/post_R009_correction.md.

candidates.statement: The claim that no frozen comparator meets the frozen service target was an artifact of unequal search spaces, and correcting it changes the answer for one comparator. The frozen design spaces let the distributed-node and added-capacity strategies search safety stock only to 90 or 120 days with no daily base-stock review, while every design-space strategy declared a search to 365 days with the review as a binary. Re-optimizing over one common inventory space, added central capacity (S4) becomes feasible for both products, reaching mean fill 0.9952 with P(fill >= 0.99) of 0.90 at 20.0 M USD/yr for norepinephrine and 23.7 M for sodium bicarbonate, against 37.8 M and 38.6 M and infeasible under its declared space. The optimizer reaches feasibility by buying inventory instead of capacity: the winning matched designs sit at 253 to 365 days of safety stock with the base-stock review on, and cost falls by 39 percent and 39 percent respectively. The distributed-node strategies improve sharply on the same correction, norepinephrine S5 from 0.9801 and 0.58 to 0.9950 and 0.85 at 20.0 M against 35.4 M, but still miss the tail requirement, and sodium bicarbonate S5 remains far short at 0.9883 and 0.58.
candidates.evidence: results/design_space/matched_20260905.json, built by scripts/run_matched_space_check.py: each named strategy optimized twice, over its declared space and over a common inventory space of safety_stock_days 30 to 365 and region_base_stock 0 or 1, 12 search runs and 40 final runs, master seed 20260901, five measured years. Compare against results/optimization/opt_20260903T220534Z/summary.json for the declared-space result
candidates.changes_design: Three consequences. First, a statement this session made, that none of the eight frozen comparators meets the frozen target while thirteen design-space cells do, is corrected: added central capacity meets it once searched fairly. Second, the ranking among feasible architectures survives on cost, since bright-stock postponement at 15.7 M and the reserve-triggered contracted network at 16.5 M remain cheaper than added capacity at 23.7 M for sodium bicarbonate, but the margin is a third rather than an order of magnitude. Third, it is now clear that in this model inventory is the cheapest route to the tail requirement for every architecture that has enough capacity, which is why the fair search finds it for all four strategies tested. Model defect MD-12 is therefore not a bookkeeping item but a comparison-validity item, and any future comparator must be searched over the same inventory space.
candidates.status: candidate; SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06 by revisions R009 to R011 and the full-resolution re-evaluation. Charging for opening inventory (NEW-1) and giving the frozen comparators the same inventory search space (MD-3, MD-12) moved the feasible set: distributed nodes now clear for norepinephrine at a tail probability of 0.940, dual sourcing clears at 0.960, and the deep-stock winners lose feasibility for sodium bicarbonate. See docs/design_space/post_R009_correction.md.

candidates.statement: Free opening inventory was carrying the architecture ranking. Until revision R009 the engine seeded opening stock at every region and site with no ledger charge, and the quantity scaled with each design's own stock policy, so a deep-stock architecture was handed roughly 1.2 million units on sodium bicarbonate, about five years of that product's structural capacity gap, inside a five-year measured window. Charging it once at production unit value drops bright-stock campaign offtake from a tail probability of 0.94 to 0.63 on that product and the reserve-triggered contracted network from 0.94 to 0.78, and both leave the feasible set. Separately, giving the frozen comparators the same inventory search space the new architectures declared for themselves (R010) makes three of the original eight feasible on at least one product, including the distributed nodes at a tail probability of 0.940 for norepinephrine. Two architectures meet the target on both products: rotating prequalified campaigns across three registered third-party lines, and dual finished-dose sourcing with an explicit key-starting-material tier.
candidates.evidence: results/optimization/opt_20260906T032432Z/ against opt_20260903T220534Z, and results/design_space/reeval_post_R009.json, which re-evaluates every incumbent design at 100 paired runs without re-searching so a classification change is attributable to the design rather than to the 40-run screen the optimization used. Three of forty cells change classification at full resolution; sixteen of forty sit within one binomial standard error of the requirement
candidates.changes_design: It is the clearest instance in the package of an accounting convention deciding an architecture comparison. Any future comparison must charge for what a design consumes at t0 and must give every architecture the same search freedom, and the study should say which of its remaining conventions could do the same thing again. It also narrows the recommendation: the shape that survives is keeping several already-registered lines warm by rotating real campaigns through them, or paying for source independence up to the starting material, rather than the cheapest deep-stock expressions that free inventory had favoured.
